# 17. Performance Optimisation

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Keep premium static sites fast, stable, and responsive through disciplined assets, minimal code, and Core Web Vitals awareness.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A performance budget for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, third-party scripts, total transfer, and request count.
- [ ] Core Web Vitals targets for LCP, CLS, and INP based on field and lab measurement where available.
- [ ] An image optimization policy for formats, dimensions, compression, responsive sources, lazy loading, and priority images.
- [ ] A font loading policy covering system fonts, self-hosted open fonts, font-display, subsets, weights, and preloads.
- [ ] A CSS delivery policy for critical styles, unused CSS control, render-blocking awareness, and media attributes.
- [ ] A JavaScript policy that favors no JS, then small deferred JS, then progressively enhanced modules.
- [ ] A third-party script budget with purpose, owner, load timing, consent rule, and removal path.
- [ ] A caching policy for immutable assets, HTML freshness, and generated files.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The largest visible content must be discoverable early and not delayed by unnecessary scripts, fonts, overlays, or lazy loading.
- [ ] Layout must reserve space for images, embeds, ads, banners, and dynamic UI to prevent shifts.
- [ ] Interactions must respond quickly and avoid long main-thread tasks.
- [ ] Static pages must not ship unused framework code for simple presentation.
- [ ] Images must be no larger than their display need at common breakpoints.
- [ ] Fonts must not block readable text or require excessive weights.
- [ ] Third-party scripts must not load before consent when consent is required.
- [ ] Performance optimizations must not damage accessibility or content quality.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check Lighthouse, WebPageTest, browser DevTools, or equivalent free tools on production-like builds.
- [ ] Check mobile throttling, not only fast desktop networks.
- [ ] Check LCP element source, preload need, fetch priority, image dimensions, and render-blocking assets.
- [ ] Check CLS sources from images, fonts, injected banners, cookie notices, and late-loading embeds.
- [ ] Check INP risks from heavy event handlers, large scripts, animation loops, and long tasks.
- [ ] Check total image folder size, unused images, duplicate formats, and oversized originals in deploy output.
- [ ] Check that analytics, maps, video embeds, chat widgets, and social embeds are delayed or replaced with static fallbacks.
- [ ] Check compression, caching, HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 support, and CDN behavior where hosting provides it.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid loading large animation, icon, slider, or UI libraries for minor effects.
- [ ] Avoid lazy-loading the LCP image.
- [ ] Avoid unbounded webfont families, weights, and character sets.
- [ ] Avoid layout shifts from missing width and height attributes.
- [ ] Avoid render-blocking third-party scripts in the head.
- [ ] Avoid performance work based only on one synthetic score.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site must feel immediate on mid-range mobile devices.
- [ ] Speed must be maintained by budgets and review gates, not one-time compression.
- [ ] Static architecture should be an advantage for performance.
- [ ] Performance reports must identify causes and actions, not only scores.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script to flag oversized assets, missing image dimensions, blocking scripts, missing lazy loading, and heavy external dependencies.
- [ ] Use optional free tools such as Lighthouse CI, WebPageTest, Squoosh CLI, sharp, or ImageMagick where appropriate.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Performance strategy: fast load, fast feel, mobile priority, minimal code/media/third-party scripts, low layout shift, responsive interactions, lightweight static hosting, and maintainability.
- [ ] Budgets cover page weight, requests, images, JavaScript, CSS, fonts, videos, embeds, analytics, and third-party scripts by page type.
- [ ] Core Web Vitals, perceived speed, HTML/CSS/JS weight, image/video/font/icon/SVG optimization, third-party scripts, analytics, forms, header/navigation, animation, layout stability, mobile, desktop, static hosting, CDN/cache, compression, lazy loading, preloading/priority, embeds, blog, portfolio/gallery, products, multilingual, accessibility/performance, SEO/performance, free tools, QA, maintenance, red flags, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] Images and media use appropriate formats, dimensions, compression, lazy loading, fallback posters, stable layout space, and no huge decorative assets.
- [ ] JavaScript is minimal, non-blocking, page-specific where useful, event listeners are efficient, scroll/resize controlled, and the site remains usable if scripts fail.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
